title: A browser uri and its positional item_path survive a Live restart and a point upgrade
question: Does the uri of a browser position stay stable across Live restarts, so that a Phase 4 cache can key on it?

answers.answered_in: A question raised in working notes kept outside the repository, under "9. Zuerst validieren". This record is the published answer.

method: A uri and an item_path were recorded 2026-09-16 against Live 12.4.5 for a device in the User Library.
Live was quit, upgraded from 12.4.5 to 12.4.6 and started again. The Control Surface selection survived the upgrade and the script answered without being reinstalled.
The same uri was looked up again 2026-09-17 against Live 12.4.6, three times: scoped to the root it lives under, scoped to a root it does not live under, and unscoped.
The recorded item_path was read back directly with lom_get.

readings.reading: uri lookup scoped to the root the item lives under
readings.note: The positional item_path came back byte for byte as recorded the day before against the previous Live version.

readings.reading: the recorded positional item_path read directly
readings.note: The positions did not shift under the upgrade either.

readings.reading: uri lookup scoped to a root the item does not live under
readings.note: A walk that finished and genuinely did not find it there, which is the correct negative for a device that lives elsewhere.
All twelve browser roots were listed as unreached. The uri did not fail to resolve; the walk never reached it.

result.means: A uri survives a Live restart and a 12.4.5 to 12.4.6 upgrade, and so does the positional item_path beside it. A cache keyed on either is viable.
result.condition: A cached entry has to carry the browser root beside the uri. Resolving a uri walks the browser again, and an unscoped walk exhausts the node budget before it arrives, which answers found: false with status: incomplete rather than an error.
result.reading_the_negative: found: false is only evidence of absence when status is complete. The unscoped reading here is the case that field exists for: without it the reply would have read as 'the uri is unstable across restarts', and the Phase 4 cache would have been designed around a defect that does not exist.

scope_and_weakness: One item, in one root, over one restart and one point upgrade. It does not show that a uri survives a major Live version, a Pack being moved, or the item being renamed.
The item is a user-library device installed by this project, so it is not evidence about factory content whose browser position Ableton controls.

provenance.twelve_roots: The count of twelve is from the reading. The root names are not: they are read off _BROWSER_ROOTS in live-remote-script/__init__.py at commit 2b19d8b, which lists instruments, sounds, drums, audio_effects, midi_effects, plugins, max_for_live, packs, user_library, clips, samples, current_project.

recorded_also_in: docs/limits.md, section 4, 'A browser uri survives a restart, and needs its root to resolve'
